website.siteDescription: Craftwork is a Philadelphia-based firm that works closely with clients to craft incredible living spaces. We build custom furniture and cabinets, design super ergonomic modern kitchens, and specialize in cast concrete countertops.

items.body: Mochi (the dog who lives in this beautiful home) has discerning tastes. He required a classic chef's kitchen with refined materials, including aged brass, marble, and herringbone oak floors. We installed a larger window and new skylight to brighten this kitchen, as well as a full set of custom cabinets to endure the ages.

mainImage.body: This partnership with Red Oak Development features our hand-troweled concrete countertops in all six units. The corner unit (pictured here) also features our custom bar and upper cabinets, as well as concrete sinks in two of the four bathrooms. The antique longleaf pine vanity is made from the beams salvaged from the church itself, with bookmatched grain wrapping the complete length of the cabinet.

This kitchen/bath renovation is a splash of midcentury modern and a splash of tiki culture. The clients wanted simple and direct materials, birch ply, concrete, rosewood pulls, with a bright color accent wall of green cement tiles. Reclaimed pieces of Dalle de Verre glass make an underlit focal point in the concrete island.

The Hawthorne House features an entirely private, one-bedroom Airbnb unit on the first floor and a private two-bedroom residence encompassing the top two floors. Between the two projects, the light-filled structure represents a continued commitment to using local, reclaimed materials. These include reclaimed wood, Pennsylvania slate, and concrete pavers made from excess concrete. Across the two units, highlights include Venitian plaster, an integrated drainboard and cutting board in the Airbnb kitchen, exposed brick, a custom staircase, pine plywood walls form the materials palette, and a master bathroom in the two-story apartment featuring a marble and slate geometric tiled floor.

The Cumberland Street rowhouse rehab was conceived as a showcase for our work. We started with a structure from the 1880s that had seen better days; once surrounded by the thriving textile industry, the neighborhood had slid into disrepair and the building was a blighted drug house for many years. Our mission was to restore the house to a modern version of its former glory. This house describes the firm’s design principles as well as our dedication to ethical and sustainable building - using reclaimed and locally sourced materials whenever possible including reclaimed interior doors throughout the house, Heart Pine flooring from a South Philly factory building, locally milled wood, and slate tile from a PA slate quarry. The cast concrete elements (countertops, windowsills, and a sink) feature inlaid glass, stone, and antique tile. The entire home itself is a reclaimed material.
